Battle of Lukaya.subject: International Relations

Battle of Lukaya.fact: On 24 February 1979, the TPDF seized Masaka.

Battle of Lukaya.fact: The swamp was impassable for vehicles, and the destruction of the causeway would delay a Tanzanian attack on Kampala for months.

Battle of Lukaya.subject: International Relations

Battle of Lukaya.fact: On 9 March over a thousand Libyan troops and about 40 Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) guerrillas belonging to Fatah were flown into Uganda.

Battle of Lukaya.subject: International Relations

Battle of Lukaya.subject: International Relations

Battle of Lukaya.subject: International Relations

Battle of Lukaya.subject: International Relations

Battle of Lukaya.fact: Radio Uganda announced the counteroffensive's beginning at noon on 9 March, while the Ugandan forces present in Lukaya withdrew. The Tanzanians and the Ugandans and Libyans were unaware of each other's positions.

Battle of Lukaya.subject: International Relations
Battle of Lukaya.question: Upon seeing the _____ at dusk, they initiated a barrage with the Katyusha rockets
Battle of Lukaya.fact: The Tanzanians and the Ugandans and Libyans were unaware of each other's positions. Upon seeing the Tanzanians at dusk, they initiated a barrage with the Katyusha rockets.

Battle of Lukaya.question: The artillery overshot them, but the mostly inexperienced _____ soldiers were frightened, and many of them broke rank and fled
Battle of Lukaya.fact: The Tanzanians and the Ugandans and Libyans were unaware of each other's positions. Upon seeing the Tanzanians at dusk, they initiated a barrage with the Katyusha rockets.

Battle of Lukaya.subject: International Relations
Battle of Lukaya.question: Despite its orders to recapture Masaka, the _____-Libyan force stopped in Lukaya, fearing that the Tanzanians were trying to bait them into an ambush
Battle of Lukaya.fact: Though others remained at their defensive positions, they were nonetheless surprised and quickly forced to withdraw into the swamp along the Masaka road after seeing the Libyan T-55s and three Ugandan M4A1 Sherman tanks advancing toward them. Despite its orders to recapture Masaka, the Ugandan-Libyan force stopped in Lukaya, fearing that the Tanzanians were trying to bait them into an ambush.

Battle of Lukaya.subject: International Relations
Battle of Lukaya.question: Only three _____ tanks guarded the road
Battle of Lukaya.fact: Despite its orders to recapture Masaka, the Ugandan-Libyan force stopped in Lukaya, fearing that the Tanzanians were trying to bait them into an ambush. Only three Tanzanian tanks guarded the road.

Battle of Lukaya.fact: The 208th Brigade under Brigadier Mwita Marwa, which was 60 kilometres (37 mi) north-west of the town, was ordered to reverse course and as quickly as possible cut off the Ugandans and Libyans from Kampala.

Battle of Lukaya.question: The 208th Brigade under _____, which was 60 kilometres (37 mi) north-west of the town, was ordered to reverse course and as quickly as possible cut off the Ugandans and Libyans from Kampala
Battle of Lukaya.fact: The 208th Brigade under Brigadier Mwita Marwa, which was 60 kilometres (37 mi) north-west of the town, was ordered to reverse course and as quickly as possible cut off the Ugandans and Libyans from Kampala.

Battle of Lukaya.fact: Oyite-Ojok and his group assumed they were allies, but then one of them said in Luo—a language not spoken in Tanzania, "Just wait until morning and we'll crush these stupid Acholi". Battle of Lukaya.fact: The regrouped 201st Brigade attacked from the front and the 208th from behind, thereby putting great pressure on the Ugandan-Libyan force.
